Subject: Production spike — 429/5xx surge and timeouts (urgent)

Aisha,

We're seeing a sustained spike of 429s and 5xx from Redwood across multiple endpoints since ~08:45 PST. Our frontend users are getting timeouts; merchant onboarding flows are failing. We've attached a short tail of the logs and a sampling of failing request IDs.

What we've observed:
- Burst of 429s starting ~08:47; soon after, clients begin retrying aggressively and we see 5xx cascades.
- Errors are concentrated on the /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints for a handful of API keys.
- We've temporarily disabled a subset of frontend instances which reduced the immediate error rate but recovery is incomplete.

We need immediate coordination: can we get a short mitigation plan and a commitment on next steps? This is hitting live payments verification and is high-severity for us.

Attachments: clearflow_prod_errors_20261208.log

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Sr. Ops Lead, ClearFlow
ops@clearflow.com

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're on it.

Immediate actions (in progress):
- We are throttling the affected API keys at the edge and enabling emergency circuit-breakers to stop client-side hammering.
- Turning on stricter per-key concurrency limits and anti-replay heuristics for the region.
- Beginning an investigation into whether this was triggered by a client-side change (SDK or config) or a traffic pattern shift.

Request for you: can you confirm whether you rolled any client SDK updates or toggled any retry settings in the last 48 hours? Any change to the frontend deploy times would help.

I'll run this as a high-priority incident and loop in execs if we see the error rate persist. Proposed 30-minute call at 09:50 PST to sync.

— Aisha

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production spike — initial hypothesis + mitigation steps

Quick summary from the triage team after looking at traces and the ClearFlow logs:

Hypothesis: an SDK-config change on ClearFlow's latest frontend rollout changed retry semantics from async/backoff with jitter to synchronous immediate retries with no jitter. When the first requests hit 429, the client code issued immediate replays which amplified the load — classic retry amplification. The customer logs show a tight retry loop with sub-200ms sleeps between attempts for some endpoints.

Evidence:
- Matching timestamps between initial 429s and client-generated replays in the logs.
- Distinctive pattern of repeated identical request payloads with incrementing attempt ids.
- No corresponding upstream capacity event on our infra prior to the amplification — suggests client-originated surge.

Short-term mitigations we applied (done):
- Emergency per-key token-bucket throttling at the edge for the affected keys (reduces request acceptance rate by ~70%).
- Enabled 429 Retry-After propagation headers and 503-backed circuit-breakers for the endpoints.
- Blacklisted one known buggy frontend build per the customer (they confirmed a rollback).

Recommended next steps (customer & platform):
- Customer: patch SDK to latest where default backoff includes exponential backoff + jitter (we identified the config diff; sending as attachment).
- Customer: roll out the SDK patch to canary hosts first; keep verbose logging on for 24 hours.
- Redwood: add a server-side short-term holdback (5s cooldown) for keys that show >X duplicates/second and surface a clear customer alert. We can push a config change to production within ~2 hours.

I'll join the 09:50 PST call and go over the log samples.

— Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sdk-config-diff.txt

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production spike — 429/5xx surge and timeouts (urgent)

Sarah — quick update and plan we can execute now: 

1) Immediate (already applied): edge throttling and circuit-breakers; per-key token-bucket limiting. Expect measurable reduction in error amplification within minutes.
2) Near-term (customer + ops): ClearFlow to roll back the frontend build or flip SDK backoff to "conservative" mode; we will provide the patch and config diff (attached). We request a canary roll for 15% of traffic and a confirmation once the canary is healthy.
3) Platform change (Redwood ops): we'll push a temporary server-side cooldown for keys exhibiting duplicate hammering (target ETA 2 hours). We'll also surface a clear error page + guidance for your engineers explaining the backoff requirement.
4) Follow-up: joint post-mortem within 72 hours and remediation timeline including improved SDK defaults and API responses recommending Retry-After semantics.

Proposed call: 09:50 PST (starting now) — joining link in the calendar invite I just sent. If that time doesn't work, propose 10:30 PST.

We realize the impact and will prioritize.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
